import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ZariskiSheaf

/-!
# The open-immersion evaluation bridge (DAT-6, stage 1)

The Zariski sheaf property of `picEt`/`pic0` landed by DAT-2
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ZariskiSheaf`) speaks *topological* covers of the test:
open sets `O i ⊆ T.left` and local data valued at affine opens subordinate to them.
The 01JJ packaging (DAT-6 stages 2–3) speaks *morphism-form* covers: families
`f i : T' i ⟶ T` of test morphisms with open-immersion left legs, jointly surjective,
carrying sections `x i : picEt C (T' i)` compatible on all common refinements.  This
file is the bridge: it evaluates a morphism-form family into DAT-2's `picEt.LocalData`
on the ranges `O i := (f i).left.opensRange` and exports the sheaf property of `picEt`
and of its degree-zero subfunctor in morphism-cover form.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.appLEAlgEquiv`: the section-ring isomorphism of an open
  immersion of tests, `Γ(T.left, V) ≃ₐ[k] Γ(T'.left, f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V)` for
  `V ≤ opensRange`, upgrading `Over.appLEAlgHom` (bijectivity:
  `Over.bijective_appLEAlgHom`, from `Scheme.Hom.isIso_app`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.coverValue`: the value at an affine open `W` subordinate to
  a cover member of the section carried by that member — evaluate at the preimage
  affine open and transport back along `appLEAlgEquiv`.  It is local data:
  `coverValue_res` (restriction within a member, pure `appLE`/`res` calculus) and
  `coverValue_glue` (agreement across members at a shared affine open, through the
  mediating test `picEt.overlapTest` — the open subscheme of the target at `W` — and
  `IsOpenImmersion.lift`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.ext_of_cover` / `picEt.existsUnique_of_cover`: **the sheaf
  property of `picEt` in morphism-cover form** — separation and unique gluing for a
  compatible family on an abstract open-immersion cover of the test.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover` /
  `pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`: the same for the degree-zero subfunctor;
  membership of the glued section is DAT-2's S-lemma (`mem_pic0Subgroup_of_cover`).

The compatibility hypothesis is the morphism form (`Presieve.Arrows.Compatible`
transported to the slice): for every pair of members and every test `Z` mapping to
both compatibly, the two restrictions of the family agree.  Stage 3 instantiates it
from a compatible family of elements of the Σ-extension on a scheme-level open cover.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-! ## The section-ring isomorphism of an open immersion of tests -/

namespace Over

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
7	
8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/
57	
58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
60	
61	universe u
62	
63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	
67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
70	
71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair
7	
8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end
141	
142	end AlgebraicGeometry
143

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/

75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:

79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88

90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)

119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.

126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been

128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),

132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/
59

61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ZariskiSheaf

/-!
# The open-immersion evaluation bridge (DAT-6, stage 1)

The Zariski sheaf property of `picEt`/`pic0` landed by DAT-2
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ZariskiSheaf`) speaks *topological* covers of the test:
open sets `O i ⊆ T.left` and local data valued at affine opens subordinate to them.
The 01JJ packaging (DAT-6 stages 2–3) speaks *morphism-form* covers: families
`f i : T' i ⟶ T` of test morphisms with open-immersion left legs, jointly surjective,
carrying sections `x i : picEt C (T' i)` compatible on all common refinements.  This
file is the bridge: it evaluates a morphism-form family into DAT-2's `picEt.LocalData`
on the ranges `O i := (f i).left.opensRange` and exports the sheaf property of `picEt`
and of its degree-zero subfunctor in morphism-cover form.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.appLEAlgEquiv`: the section-ring isomorphism of an open
  immersion of tests, `Γ(T.left, V) ≃ₐ[k] Γ(T'.left, f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V)` for
  `V ≤ opensRange`, upgrading `Over.appLEAlgHom` (bijectivity:
  `Over.bijective_appLEAlgHom`, from `Scheme.Hom.isIso_app`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.coverValue`: the value at an affine open `W` subordinate to
  a cover member of the section carried by that member — evaluate at the preimage
  affine open and transport back along `appLEAlgEquiv`.  It is local data:
  `coverValue_res` (restriction within a member, pure `appLE`/`res` calculus) and
  `coverValue_glue` (agreement across members at a shared affine open, through the
  mediating test `picEt.overlapTest` — the open subscheme of the target at `W` — and
  `IsOpenImmersion.lift`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.ext_of_cover` / `picEt.existsUnique_of_cover`: **the sheaf
  property of `picEt` in morphism-cover form** — separation and unique gluing for a
  compatible family on an abstract open-immersion cover of the test.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover` /
  `pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`: the same for the degree-zero subfunctor;
  membership of the glued section is DAT-2's S-lemma (`mem_pic0Subgroup_of_cover`).

The compatibility hypothesis is the morphism form (`Presieve.Arrows.Compatible`
transported to the slice): for every pair of members and every test `Z` mapping to
both compatibly, the two restrictions of the family agree.  Stage 3 instantiates it
from a compatible family of elements of the Σ-extension on a scheme-level open cover.
-/

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
7	
8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/
57	
58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
60	
61	universe u
62	
63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	
67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
70	
71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the

producer should quote.

the supplied chart class is classified by that chart's own morphism to `DivScheme`*.

which is gated on the G-4 certificate discharge. -/

    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83

85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end

/-- **The unit of the étale sheafification** (gap G4 of the (C2) recon): the natural
transformation from the honest relative Picard functor into the étale-sheafified
Layer-2 functor.  On affine tests it is the unit of the plus construction
(`picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`); its affine components are injective by the (C1)
étale separatedness (`PicEtAff.unit_injective`), and bijective over section-admitting
tests by the (C2) comparison. -/
def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicToPicEt C T.unop)
  naturality T T' g := by
    ext z
    exact (picEtMap_relPicToPicEt C g.unop z).symm

/-- **The unit of the étale sheafification** (gap G4 of the (C2) recon): the natural
transformation from the honest relative Picard functor into the étale-sheafified
Layer-2 functor.  On affine tests it is the unit of the plus construction
(`picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`); its affine components are injective by the (C1)
étale separatedness (`PicEtAff.unit_injective`), and bijective over section-admitting
tests by the (C2) comparison. -/
def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicToPicEt C T.unop)
  naturality T T' g := by
    ext z
    exact (picEtMap_relPicToPicEt C g.unop z).symm

@[simp]
lemma picEtUnit_app (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (z : relPic C T.unop) :
    (picEtUnit C).app T z = relPicToPicEt C T.unop z :=
  rfl

/-- Affine consistency of the unit, natural-transformation form. -/
theorem picEtAffineEquiv_picEtUnit_app (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (z : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
    picEtAffineEquiv C A ((picEtUnit C).app (op (overSpec k A)) z)
      = PicEtAff.unit C A z :=
  picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A z

end unit

/-- **The unit of the étale sheafification** (gap G4 of the (C2) recon): the natural
transformation from the honest relative Picard functor into the étale-sheafified
Layer-2 functor.  On affine tests it is the unit of the plus construction
(`picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`); its affine components are injective by the (C1)
étale separatedness (`PicEtAff.unit_injective`), and bijective over section-admitting
tests by the (C2) comparison. -/
def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicToPicEt C T.unop)
  naturality T T' g := by
    ext z
    exact (picEtMap_relPicToPicEt C g.unop z).symm

@[simp]
lemma picEtUnit_app (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (z : relPic C T.unop) :
    (picEtUnit C).app T z = relPicToPicEt C T.unop z :=
  rfl

/-- Affine consistency of the unit, natural-transformation form. -/
theorem picEtAffineEquiv_picEtUnit_app (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (z : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
    picEtAffineEquiv C A ((picEtUnit C).app (op (overSpec k A)) z)
      = PicEtAff.unit C A z :=
  picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A z

end unit
